US8069128B2.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering.description: A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.

Classification Model.description: A model generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, maintained exclusively in non-persistent memory on a user's client device and not stored on disk or in any persistent data store.

First Message Filter.description: A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store.

Second Multi-Pass Message Filter.description: A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis, perform a second pass on sorted messages to generate misclassification identification, and be trained based on which folder each message resides.

Network Device.description: A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform first and second pass analyses, display misclassification identification, and purge the classification model from non-persistent memory.

Transceiver.description: A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.

Processor.description: A component of the network device operative to perform actions including first pass analysis, second pass analysis, displaying misclassification identification, and purging the classification model.

Message Folders.description: A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter, used to train the multi-pass message filter.

Misclassification Identification.description: An identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, generated by the second pass and displayed so that misclassified messages can be moved to a different folder.

Non-Persistent Memory Location.description: A memory location where the generated classification model resides exclusively, from which the model is purged and not stored on disk or another persistent data store.

Persistent Store.description: A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.

Processor Readable Storage Medium.description: A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.

Client Device.description: A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may occur entirely.

Sender Information.description: Information within messages read during the first pass, including sender address and whether the sender's address is in an address book associated with a recipient.

Message Headers.description: Information within messages read during the first pass, including a subject and an originating network address.

Message Contents.description: The contents of messages read during the first pass analysis.

Attachments.description: Attachments within messages read during the first pass analysis.

Address Book.description: An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis to generate the classification model.

First Classification Data.description: Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.

Second Classification Data.description: Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, residing exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and used to score messages in the second pass.

Message Score.description: A score assigned to each message by the second pass of the multi-pass message filter, used to identify messages sorted into an incorrect folder.
